subject: unmodeled error covariances among endogenous variables in a path model

messages.author: 706883a2e98a8b22
messages.subject: unmodeled error covariances among endogenous variables in a path model
parts:
Hi,

When the dependence relation between two endogenous variables in a path model is unmodeled, the function sem() automatically sets to zero their error covariance. This makes sense to me.
However, there is an exception : when the two endogenous variables do not predict any other variable in the path model, and their relation is unmodeled, their error covariance is automatically considered a free parameter.

My question is : Why ? AMOS, for example, at my knowledge sets to zero their error covariance even in this case.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: unmodeled error covariances among endogenous variables in a path model
parts:
Why ?

Why not?  It seems unreasonable to expect that a set of common predictors will ever explain 100% of why 2 variables correlate (unless it is a design feature).  My interpretation is that residuals are expected to covary, but we cannot be sure the model would be identified if we allowed residuals of mediators to correlate.  So it requires the researcher to consider the model more carefully and manually free them when appropriate (e.g., parallel mediators, but not serial mediators).

You can control this ?lavOptions by setting auto.cov.y=FALSE
